checks.rule: The Environment Agency composite DTM covers about 99 percent of England at 1 m spatial resolution.
The DTM removes surface objects from DSM data to model terrain surface.
The 2022 composite merges Time Stamped archive and National LIDAR Programme surveys.
Where repeat surveys exist the newest best-resolution data is used in the composite.
Resampled source data uses bilinear interpolation before merging.
Composite source surveys span 6 June 2000 through 2 April 2022 for the published 2022 product.
Composite tiles are GeoTIFF rasters aligned to the OS National Grid.
Elevations are presented in metres referenced to Ordnance Survey Newlyn using OSTN15 transformation.
Individual LIDAR surveys entering the composite have vertical accuracy of plus or minus 15 cm RMSE.
Do not treat 1 m spatial resolution as 1 m vertical accuracy; vertical error is tracked separately.
A parcel result must retain source-survey date and metadata-index provenance because composite cells can originate from different survey epochs.
No height-difference row is promoted unless the parcel geometry intersects actual available composite coverage.
